query: For a high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution and exhibiting a favorable strength–ductility combination, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading? Explain the hypothesized mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the same alloy tested under identical conditions without the intervention, define the applicable exposure and loading regime, identify supporting evidence from prior observations, and specify an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a controlled amount of grain boundary pinning particles will preserve toughness in a high-entropy alloy after thermal exposure and subsequent loading.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase solid solution high-entropy alloy with a favorable strength–ductility combination
generation.intervention: Introduction of grain boundary pinning particles
generation.conditions: Thermal exposure at 800°C for 100 hours followed by tensile loading at room temperature
generation.mechanism: The grain boundary pinning particles will inhibit grain growth and reduce the formation of detrimental precipitates during thermal exposure, thereby preserving the alloy's toughness
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy with grain boundary pinning particles will exhibit higher toughness compared to the same alloy without the intervention, tested under identical conditions
generation.baseline: Toughness of the alloy without grain boundary pinning particles, tested under identical conditions
generation.boundary: Thermal exposure temperature and duration, as well as loading rate and magnitude
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and type of grain boundary pinning particles, as well as the potential effects of particle distribution and morphology

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the toughness of high-entropy alloys with and without grain boundary pinning particles after thermal exposure and loading
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with grain boundary pinning particles exhibits lower or equivalent toughness compared to the alloy without the intervention, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Abstract Concurrent strength–ductility improvement of HfMoTaTiZr is achieved via Cr addition and the underlying strengthening mechanism was discussed. 4.2 at% Cr addition into HfMoTaTiZr led to the formation of a Laves phase, in addition to the BCC phase. The hardness of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 is 535.8 Hv 0.3 , 56.96% higher than the reference alloy HfMoTaTiZr. The yield strength and fracture strain of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 reach 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%, respectively, 207.5 MPa and 20.6% higher than HfMoTaTiZr. Solid solution hardening and the presence of the intermetallic Laves phase are believed to be responsible for the enhancement in strength and the formation of a reticulated structure of the Laves phase in HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 results in the improvement in ductility.

Abstract A NbMoTaWVTi refractory high entropy alloy (HEA) has been successfully synthesized by mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS). The microstructure and mechanical properties of this alloy are investigated. It is observed that only two types of body-centered cubic (BCC) solid solutions are formed in the powders after ball milling for 40 h. However, a new face-centered cubic (FCC) precipitated phase is observed in the BCC matrix of bulk material consolidated by SPS. The FCC precipitated phase is identified as TiO, due to the introduction of O during the preparing process of HEA. The compressive yield strength, fracture strength, and total fracture strain of the consolidated bulk HEA are 2709 MPa, 3115 MPa, and 11.4%, respectively. The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles. Keywords: refractory high entropy alloy, microstructure, mechanical properties
